description.from:
As a Claude Code or Gemini editor working from a story ID and a Papyrus sign-in, I want to create, compare, revise and apply an OpenAI illustration using the publication's resolved visual guidelines, so the same workflow works from another agent session without reconstructing the art direction from chat history.

This is the end-to-end acceptance story for the existing CLI (PPY-40b7a4), generation and review (PPY-6f9fb9), OpenAI adapter (PPY-9087be) and image-work skill (PPY-876957). Consume the published visual guidelines from PPY-2a2a8a and the profile/example records from PPY-6d878b. Claude and Gemini are CLI callers in this story. OpenAI is the image provider, with its credential and spending settings held by Papyrus. The Gemini image provider remains PPY-c7a616.

Feature: Reproduce the publication's illustration workflow from a signed-in terminal

  Scenario: Preview the plan from a story and the publication's visual guidelines
    Given an agent can edit the story and the publication has a versioned illustration profile with approved style examples
    When the agent previews an illustration brief with the CLI
    Then the CLI returns the resolved image type, profile version, the plan for each candidate, example identifiers, allowed output sizes and a cost estimate without spending
    And the plan includes the publication palette, relevant composition rules and its binding prohibition on realistic or photorealistic generated images
    And the plan can be inspected from a session with no site checkout or prior chat

  Scenario: Request one image or four alternatives with the appropriate approval
    Given OpenAI is configured and the publication has approved spending
    When the agent requests one image under the configured policy or a person authorizes a round of four
    Then the CLI returns a round ID and one or four candidate IDs respectively
    And a completed four-option round gives the editor four separately previewable images with distinguishable compositions
    And an unattended request for four returns the documented approval requirement before any spend
    And the candidate record identifies the actual model, lane, prompt and profile version used

  Scenario: Refine the chosen candidate and apply the required variants to a draft
    Given a selected illustration candidate and a publication that requires Day and Night art for this image type
    When the agent uses the candidate as an image reference and prepares the Night version
    Then it preserves the composition and follows the publication's Night palette and foreground contrast
    And both images can be previewed before the pair is applied to the same draft version with alt text and generation provenance
    And applying the pair records the publication's configured review status and leaves the live story unchanged
    And the draft's cover and share preview use the publication's designated variants

  Scenario: Explain missing capabilities before any spend
    Given the provider is disabled, the requested operation is unavailable, or the configured model cannot satisfy the requested output
    When the agent previews or requests the round
    Then it gets an actionable machine-readable result naming the missing capability or required approval
    And no provider or model is silently substituted

The image-work skill should give one complete example with the real CLI syntax, sample brief, prompt preview, polling and preview URLs, choice or iteration, and draft application. Include a documented fallback using locally generated files and `papyrus stories save-version --images`, with matching Day/Night asset names where required. The existing upload route was used successfully on Machines on Machines. Prove the signed-in CLI flow with recorded provider responses and verify a representative approved Day/Night cover locally. Reuse PPY-99dcfa for rendering and PPY-74ef89 for drawn figures. Do not fold figure rendering or the Gemini image provider into this acceptance story.
description.to:
As a Claude Code or Gemini editor working from a Story ID and a Papyrus sign-in, I want to create, compare, revise and apply an OpenAI illustration using the publication's resolved visual guidelines, so the same workflow works from another agent session without reconstructing the art direction from chat history.

This is the end-to-end acceptance story for the existing CLI (PPY-40b7a4), generation and review (PPY-6f9fb9), OpenAI adapter (PPY-9087be) and image-work skill (PPY-876957). Consume the published visual guidelines from PPY-2a2a8a and the profile/example records from PPY-6d878b. Claude and Gemini are CLI callers. OpenAI is the image provider, with its credential and spending settings held by Papyrus. The Gemini image provider remains PPY-c7a616.

Proposed CLI shape. Names are illustrative until the shared operation table is updated.

```sh
# One composition, with Day followed by a reference-based Night edit.
papyrus images generate --story STORY --use cover --brief "..." --theme-pair

# Three or four Day concepts for the editor to compare.
papyrus images generate --story STORY --use cover --brief "..." --count 4
papyrus images round ROUND

# The editor picked option B (option 2). Generate only its Night image.
papyrus images variant --round ROUND --option B --theme night

# Low-level file workflow for local art and scripts.
papyrus images variant --input cover.png --output cover.dark.png --theme night
papyrus stories save-version --story STORY --body-file body.md --reason "Add cover" --images ./art
```

Feature: Reproduce the publication's illustration workflow from a signed-in terminal

  Scenario: Preview the plan from a Story and the publication's visual guidelines
    Given an agent can edit the Story and the publication has a versioned illustration profile with approved style examples
    When the agent previews an illustration brief with the CLI
    Then the CLI returns the resolved image type, profile version, plans, example IDs, allowed sizes and a cost estimate without spending
    And the plan includes the publication palette, composition rules and binding constraints, including the ban on realistic or photorealistic generation for Machines on Machines
    And the plan can be inspected from a session with no site checkout or prior chat

  Scenario: Generate a matched Day and Night pair in one command
    Given the publication allows OpenAI generation for this image type and the caller is authorized for both image operations
    When the caller requests one composition as a Day and Night pair
    Then Papyrus queues one tracked job and returns its ID and the combined cost estimate
    And Papyrus generates Day first and supplies that exact asset as the reference for the Night edit
    And the Night image retains the composition and crop and uses the profile's Night palette and foreground contrast
    And both previews and their source relationship are available from the same job ID without local filenames
    And if only the Night edit fails, retrying it uses the saved Day asset

  Scenario: Generate one set of three or four Day options
    Given a person has authorized this specific round under the publication's spending policy
    When the agent requests three or four alternatives in one call
    Then Papyrus queues that number of Day options and returns one round ID
    And each option has a preview and a stable label A through C or A through D, with its numeric position
    And labels stay attached to their original options as images finish or are retried
    And the options offer distinguishable compositions and the round queues no Night edits
    And an agent request without the required one-round approval returns the documented approval requirement before spending

  Scenario: Generate Night for only the option the editor chose
    Given the editor picked B from a Day round with stable option labels
    When the agent requests a Night variant for B using the round ID and option label or its numeric position 2
    Then Papyrus resolves B's stored Day image and queues exactly one Night edit that references it
    And A, C and any D remain unchanged
    And Papyrus links the Night result and both previews to B so the same selection can apply the pair together
    And asking again while B's Night job is pending or ready returns that job or result unless the caller explicitly requests a new edit
    And an unknown option or a Day option that is not ready returns an actionable error before spending

  Scenario: Apply the selected pair to the draft
    Given the selected Day option and its Night variant are ready
    When the agent applies the pair from its round and option or durable candidate ID
    Then both assets are applied to the same draft version with alt text and generation provenance
    And the draft's cover and share preview use the publication's designated variants
    And the publication's review policy applies and the live story stays unchanged

  Scenario: Use the low-level file workflow
    Given the editor has a local Day image and wants to manage files directly
    When the editor supplies the Day file and a Night output filename
    Then the CLI edits the supplied image using the resolved Night guidelines and writes the requested output file
    And the two files can be uploaded together with the existing save-version --images workflow

  Scenario: Explain missing capabilities before spending
    Given the provider is disabled, the requested operation is unavailable, or the configured model cannot satisfy the requested output
    When the agent previews or requests generation
    Then it gets an actionable machine-readable result naming the missing capability or required approval
    And no provider or model is silently substituted

Use the same provider, tenant, review and spending checks for the convenience commands and file operations. Record the actual model, lane, prompt and profile version for each generated image. One pair is one composition with two image operations, so its cost preview covers both and the publication's spend policy applies to both. Include the three routes in the image-work skill: one pair in one command, Day options then Night for the picked option, and direct file-based editing and upload. Prove the signed-in flow with recorded provider responses and verify one approved Day/Night cover locally. Reuse PPY-99dcfa for rendering and PPY-74ef89 for drawn figures.
